data.narrative:
MineSense Technologies is a Growth-stage frontier-tech company operating in Climate & Energy, having raised $100M+. The comparable universe comprises 1 public company and 8 private peers in the Climate & Energy sector, though no peers were sufficiently similar in stage and valuation tier to form a reliable narrow peer set for median-based valuation.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable and generates a point estimate of $120M. This method takes the $100M total raised as a value proxy and applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-stage advancement. Given the lack of sufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables in the Climate & Energy sector, peer-median triangulation was not viable—the broader sector set of 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (LNZA) lacks the homogeneity needed for reliable multiple extraction.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $102M to $138M, centered on $120M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodology; the low and high bounds represent modest sensitivity around the stage-progression point estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of transaction multiples from sufficiently similar Growth-stage peers and limited visibility into MineSense's unit economics relative to the reference set. Investors should require additional disclosure on revenue trajectory, unit contribution margin, or recent third-party valuations to narrow this range or validate the stage-progression assumption.
